acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer is ready to run the FR-10 enable/disable/behavioral-rollback/re-enable lifecycle and has a recorded Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

oracle.expected: The Consumer completes re-enable through its real repository call surface and restores the recorded Prior Route identity plus verdict/diagnostic baseline.
forbidden: Re-enable is performed only through a simulated, indirect, or nonexistent call surface.
The Prior Route identity or verdict/diagnostic baseline is not restored.
oracle.observable: The lifecycle test records the real Consumer call surface, completed re-enable operation, and comparison with the recorded Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

acceptance.then: The applicable Consumer has completed re-enable through a real call surface with the Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline restored.
acceptance.when: The FR-10 enable/disable/behavioral-rollback/re-enable flow is executed through the repository Toolchain.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise an applicable Consumer with a simulated, indirect, or missing re-enable call surface, or with a non-restored Prior Route identity or verdict/diagnostic baseline.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain lifecycle verification invoke every applicable Consumer's real call surface for enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable, then compare the restored Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The verification change is reversible and preserves Consumer route state and existing evidence schemas.

slice_hint.state_transition: Applicable Consumer pending re-enable -> real-call-surface re-enable completed -> Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline restored.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted lifecycle test proves every applicable Consumer used a real call surface for re-enable and restored its Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

acceptance.given: The supported Acceptance package route definitions and their Toolchain route implementation are present before route-set evaluation.

oracle.expected: Each supported Acceptance package route remains present and callable, and successful evidence binds the effective inspected content.
forbidden: The supported Acceptance package routes become unavailable or are removed from the supported route set.
Successful evidence is not bound to the effective inspected content.
oracle.observable: The package validation test enumerates supported Acceptance routes, calls them through the Toolchain, and inspects successful-evidence binding to effective inspected content.

acceptance.then: Supported Acceptance package routes remain available and their successful evidence binds effective inspected content.
acceptance.when: The supported route set is evaluated through package validation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Remove, make uncallable, or detach effective-inspected-content binding from a supported Acceptance package route and run package validation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve supported Acceptance package route availability and bind every successful route result to its effective inspected content in Toolchain package validation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The verification change is reversible and preserves existing package-route and evidence-binding schema compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Supported Acceptance routes available -> routes evaluated -> callable route successes bound to effective inspected content.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted package test confirms every supported Acceptance route is present and callable and every success binds effective inspected content.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain success outcome is pending evaluation with identity and execution facts that may be unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable.

oracle.expected: Success is permitted only after the Toolchain verifies identity and execution facts.
forbidden: A success outcome is reported while identity or execution facts cannot be verified.
Unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable identity or execution facts permit success.
oracle.observable: The semantic-gate evaluation records verified identity and execution facts for success, or blocks success with the applicable unverifiable-fact reason.

acceptance.then: Success remains blocked until identity and execution facts are verifiable.
acceptance.when: A Toolchain success outcome is evaluated by the semantic gate.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Supply unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable identity or execution facts to a candidate success evaluation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the Toolchain semantic gate to reject candidate success whenever identity or execution facts are unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The gate remains backward compatible for verifiable success facts; reverting restores prior success-evaluation behavior without state migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Candidate success with potentially unverifiable facts -> semantic-gate evaluation -> success allowed only with verifiable identity and execution facts.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The semantic handoff negative selector rejects every candidate success with unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable identity or execution facts.

acceptance.given: A target package is selected for Toolchain inspection and its identity has not yet been independently verified.

oracle.expected: Before effective inspection, an independent target-package identity verification result is produced and effective inspection proceeds only for that verified target.
forbidden: Target package identity is treated as verified without an independent verification.
Effective inspection proceeds for a missing, illegal, unsupported, escaping, substituted, or wrong target.
oracle.observable: The replay validation result contains the separately produced target-package identity verification and effective-inspection target binding.

acceptance.then: Target package identity has been independently verified before effective inspection.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain verifies a selected target package before effective inspection.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run replay verification with a missing, illegal, unsupported, escaping, substituted, or wrong target, or without an independent identity-verification result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require Toolchain replay validation to independently verify the selected target package identity before effective inspection and fail closed for missing, illegal, unsupported, escaping, substituted, or wrong targets.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The verifier change is reversible and preserves existing replay-evidence schema compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Selected target with unverified identity -> independent identity verification -> effective inspection of the verified target only.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Replay validation produces an independent target identity verification before effective inspection and rejects missing, illegal, unsupported, escaping, substituted, and wrong targets.
